items.label: f01-p2025-only
items.front: Why should updateTask/deleteTask catch only Prisma error P2025 instead of every error?
items.back: P2025 is 'record not found' - the only failure that truly means 404. Catching everything turns outages and bugs into 404s; rethrowing the rest lets the route answer 500.

items.label: f03-envelope
items.front: What response envelope does the tasks router promise for success and for errors?
items.back: Success: { data: ... }. Error: { error: "message", details?: ... } - one consistent shape the frontend can rely on.

items.label: f02-routes-vs-services
items.front: In grokbuildjs, what belongs in routes/ versus services/?
items.back: Routes own HTTP concerns: validation, status codes, response shape. Services own business logic and Prisma data access, so they can be tested and swapped independently.

items.prompt: When the backend answers the Complete request with 400 { error, details }, what does the frontend's updateTask(id, data) resolve to?

choices.text: undefined: fetch does not reject on a 400, and the error body has no data field
It rejects with the 400 status: fetch throws, so the mutation's onError handler runs
It never resolves: the error response body is never consumed
The error object: json.data falls back to the whole response body

choices: undefined: fetch does not reject on a 400, and the error body has no data field
It rejects with the 400 status: fetch throws, so the mutation's onError handler runs
It never resolves: the error response body is never consumed
The error object: json.data falls back to the whole response body

items.explanation: updateTask never checks res.ok. A failed update therefore looks like a successful mutation that returned nothing - one reason the Complete bug is easy to miss in the UI.

items.prompt: The frontend's Complete button sends PUT /api/tasks/1 with the body { "completed": true }. What does the committed backend answer?

choices.text: 500 Failed to update task: completed is not a known database column
200 with the task marked completed: PUT accepts partial bodies, like PATCH does
400 Validation failed: PUT parses with createTaskSchema, which needs a title
404 Task not found: the update service swallows the validation error

choices: 500 Failed to update task: completed is not a known database column
200 with the task marked completed: PUT accepts partial bodies, like PATCH does
400 Validation failed: PUT parses with createTaskSchema, which needs a title
404 Task not found: the update service swallows the validation error

items.explanation: PUT reuses createTaskSchema (title: z.string().min(1)). A body without title fails parse, the ZodError branch returns 400. The README's 'Before You Try to Run It' list calls this out.

items.prompt: updateTask spreads data and then sets dueDate: data.dueDate ? new Date(data.dueDate) : undefined. When the request omits dueDate, what happens to the stored due date?

choices.text: It is set to the current time: the fallback branch calls new Date() for it
It is cleared to NULL: undefined is written into the column as a missing value
The update fails: dueDate is required whenever any update data is sent
It is left unchanged: Prisma treats an undefined update field as 'do not touch'

choices: It is set to the current time: the fallback branch calls new Date() for it
It is cleared to NULL: undefined is written into the column as a missing value
The update fails: dueDate is required whenever any update data is sent
It is left unchanged: Prisma treats an undefined update field as 'do not touch'

items.explanation: In Prisma, undefined means the field is omitted from the update, while null would clear it. createTask, by contrast, writes null explicitly when no dueDate is given.

items.prompt: Why does the committed backend fail before it ever serves a request?

choices.text: The Prisma schema has no Task model, so the Prisma client cannot be generated at install
PORT is required in the environment and has no default value in index.ts
index.ts imports cors, but no cors entry is listed in backend/package.json dependencies
express.json() is never registered, so the startup validation step fails

500 Failed to delete task: the route's own catch block sends that status
503 Service Unavailable: Prisma reports that the database server is down

items.prompt: A client works around the bug by sending PUT with { "title": "Same title", "completed": true }. What happens to the task's completed flag?

choices.text: The request fails with 400: completed is an unrecognized key in the schema
It becomes true: the schema keeps completed but resets the title to an empty default
It stays unchanged: validation passes, but Zod strips the unknown completed key
It becomes true: the title requirement is now satisfied, so completed is passed on

items.explanation: z.object() drops keys it does not declare by default; createTaskSchema declares only title, description and dueDate. PHASE2 0.2 points out this second, quieter failure.
